back: A compound containing radioactive nuclei, introduced into the body and absorbed by the tissue studied; its emissions are detected outside the body.
Positrons annihilate with electrons, giving two gamma photons that leave the body.
A particle and its antiparticle meet; their mass becomes photon energy, with mass-energy, momentum and charge conserved.
Zero initial momentum: the photons' momenta (E/c) must cancel.
Photons arriving at opposite detectors within a few ns are paired; the annihilation lies on the line joining them.
$x = \dfrac{c\,\Delta t}{2}$ from the midpoint, towards the detector that fired first
β⁺ emitter, half-life about 110 minutes, attached to a glucose-like molecule absorbed by active tissue.
A computer combines millions of lines of response to map tracer concentration in 3D.
